title: feat(plugin-audit): sys_comment_reaction, the reactor's own record of an emoji reaction
body:
Fixes #22566
Clause-②: yes

The additive half of ruling A, amended, on #22505 (director record `6091550406`, delegated judgment `6091621568`), scoped by triage `6092508551` and claim `6092717444`. A new object, `sys_comment_reaction`, holds one emoji reaction per row, and the row belongs to the user who reacted. The retirement of `sys_comment.reactions` is #22573 and is not touched here: the field, its description and its bundles are byte-identical. #22500 remains open; it waits on the full ruling, not on this PR.

**Why the first line is `Part of`.** One piece of the card's scope cannot be built as the card words it, so it is back with the seat as a decision (see "Who grants the bits" below). Everything else the card scopes is in this diff. If the decision lands on option B, nothing here changes and the first line can be rewritten to close the card.

## What this adds

- **The object** (`plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-comment-reaction.object.ts`, registered beside `sys_comment` in `AuditPlugin.init` and provisioned with it). Fields: `comment_id` (text, at most 255 characters), `emoji` (text, at most 64), `user_id` (lookup to `sys_user`), `created_at`. `apiMethods: ['get', 'list', 'create', 'delete']`; `userActions: { edit: false, import: false }`; `feeds: false`, `activities: false`. No `sharingModel`, and the audit columns are injected, so `created_by` exists and is stamped.
- **Read rule.** A reaction is readable exactly when its comment is. Details below.
- **Create rule.** A caller reacts only to a comment it can read; a comment it cannot read, or one that does not exist, is refused with `403 RECORD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` (the comment gate's own code, no new code). `user_id` is stamped from the session, and a value the client sends is replaced. A session with no user is refused.
- **Delete rule.** No new code. The row is the reactor's own, so the platform's own-record floor, `owner_only_deletes` (`created_by == current_user.id`, positions `org_member`), is the whole rule: a member deletes their own reaction and not another member's. No moderation-style alternate match is contributed for reactions.
- **Update.** Not offered (`apiMethods`). A reaction is deleted and made again.
- The tenancy census and the plugin-audit translation bundles are regenerated by their generators (`platform-object-tenancy-census.mjs --write`, `check-i18n-bundles.mjs --write --filter=audit`). The zh-CN, ja-JP and es-ES leaves are the generator's source fills, with provenance records.

## The read rule, and why this one

Measured options:

1. **`controlled_by_parent` on a `master_detail` to `sys_comment`.** Rejected. ADR-0055 §3 makes every write to a detail require EDIT on its master, and a member cannot edit another member's comment (the author-only floor), so it would refuse exactly the reaction the ruling admits. Its read half is also the wrong question: the master set comes from the master's RLS and sharing filters, which never run the comment's thread gate, because that gate is an engine middleware, not a row policy.
2. **A copy of the thread rule on reactions.** Ruled out by the card.
3. **Chosen: ask the comment.** The comment gate's two installers in `comment-access-hooks.ts` now answer for `sys_comment_reaction` too, with the same handler registered on both objects. The reaction read gate pre-scans the candidate `comment_id`s under system context, then hands them to `resolveReadableParentIds` as one caller-scoped read of `sys_comment`. That read runs everything a direct read of those comments runs: the caller's grant on `sys_comment`, its row scope, and the thread gate, which in turn asks the record each thread names. The result is ANDed into the reaction query as `comment_id` `$in`. It covers `find`, `findOne`, `count` and `aggregate`. Analytics routes the object through the engine, because it carries an object middleware. The create gate asks the same evaluator, so the create door never admits a reaction the read door would hide.

Why one handler per seam and not one per object: the system and context-less exemption each installer opens with is read once for both objects. The `isSystem` census (`check:system-context-census`) stays at 123 read sites, with no new anchor needed.

## Uniqueness

`(comment_id, emoji, user_id)` is one row, held by a declared unique index with its scope spelled out (`unique: 'organization'`, ADR-0120 D1). That is the platform's existing answer. A second identical reaction is refused by the store: the engine envelope is `DUPLICATE_RECORD` 409, and the data door answers it as `409 UNIQUE_VIOLATION`, pinned through `mapDataError`. Two members reacting at once keep two rows. No new error code.

## Why `comment_id` is an id column and not a lookup

Referential behaviour on delete runs as the caller (`cascadeDeleteRelations` recurses with the caller's context; the `cascade` arm is excluded from the referential-clear exemption by ruling). A `cascade` lookup would make an author's delete of their own comment delete other members' reactions under the author's authority, and the own-record floor refuses that. A required `set_null` lookup escalates to `restrict`. Either would stop an author deleting their own comment once someone had reacted. So `comment_id` is an id column, like `sys_comment.thread_id`. A deleted comment's reactions stay in storage and are read by nobody, because the read gate fails closed on a comment that no longer exists. This is pinned.

## Who grants the bits: the open decision

The card asks for "permission-set rows (create, read, delete-own)". Measured on `origin/main` `25be87612d`:

- The shape mechanism hypothesis 2 points at does not exist. `default-permission-sets.ts` `:1164`–`:1218` is the `sys_comment_moderation` delete alternate and nothing else. The platform ships no create or read bit on `sys_comment`. An app grants those: hotcrm's members comment because objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2043 grants `sys_comment` read, create and edit. The showcase and CRM examples grant members nothing on `sys_comment`.
- The only shipped set every member resolves is `member_default`, the `everyone` baseline. ADR-0090 D5 hard-blocks `allowDelete` there. `describeHighPrivilegeBits` would answer "delete/purge/transfer on 'sys_comment_reaction'", `bindBaselineToEveryone` would then refuse to bind the whole baseline, and `audience-anchor-set-claims.pin.test.ts` pins `member_default` anchor-safe. So no shipped set can hand every member a delete bit.
- The "delete-own" half needs no row: `owner_only_deletes` already does it (pinned below).

Options, which the report on #22566 sets out on the four axes:

- **A.** `member_default` grants read and create on reactions (anchor-safe), and delete stays app-granted. A member on an app that grants no delete can add a reaction and never remove it.
- **B. This diff as it stands.** No platform grant: an app grants read, create and delete on `sys_comment_reaction` wherever it grants `sys_comment`, and the platform's floor keeps the delete to the reactor's own row. A missing grant fails loudly on first use, for adding and removing alike.
- **C.** Amend ADR-0090 D5 to admit an owner-scoped delete bit on an `everyone`-bound set, then grant all three in `member_default`. This is a Tier H ADR plus a `packages/spec` predicate change.

Recommended: B. The changeset states the B posture and says the baseline grants nothing.

## Census of `sys_comment.reactions` consumers (report only, no edits)

- **objectstack** (`git grep reactions` over the tree at this head): the field's declaration (`plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-comment.object.ts`) and the four generated bundles. No runtime reader or writer. `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts` `enableReactions` (`RecordActivityProps`) is a feed display toggle that reads no column, so it is a different surface and stays out.
- **objectui** `main` `d758f2f20d`: one reader and one writer, both `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx`. The read is `dataSource.find('sys_comment', …)` at `:1907`, parsing `c.reactions` at `:1920`. The write is `update('sys_comment', id, { reactions: JSON.stringify(…) })` at `:2254`–`:2255`. Downstream renderers take the parsed value, never the column: `plugin-detail` `RecordActivityTimeline.tsx` and `ReactionPicker.tsx` (`FeedItem.reactions`, `types/src/views.ts:650`). `collaboration/src/CommentThread.tsx:25` takes a `reactions` prop, and no in-repo caller feeds it. At the pinned `.objectui-sha` `47b1f0bb71` the same single site appears at `:1884`, `:1897` and `:2226`–`:2227`.
- **cloud**: NOT MEASURED (no access from this session). The director's reading (`6091621568`) is that cloud has no reader.
- This confirms the director's finding: objectui's chatter is the only reader and the only writer. #22573 reads this.

## Tests

- `plugin-audit/src/comment-reaction-access.integration.test.ts` (real kernel, real `ObjectQLPlugin`, real SQLite driver, `AuditPlugin`). For every caller, the comments its readable reactions point at equal the reacted comments it can read. It also pins `find`, `count`, `findOne` and `aggregate`; the reader's one batched `comment_id` `$in` read, which makes one comment probe per read and never one per row; the create refusals on an unreadable comment, a missing comment, an empty `comment_id` and a session with no user (`code` plus `status`); `user_id` and `created_by` stamped with the reactor; two concurrent reactions kept as two rows; the duplicate refused as 409 and mapped to `UNIQUE_VIOLATION`; and a comment's author deleting the comment with others' reactions on it.
- `plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-comment-reaction.object.test.ts` holds the declaration to what the other rules read: no `sharingModel`, audit columns on, `comment_id` with no reference or delete behaviour, the index and its scope, `apiMethods` without `update`, and no managed-affordance conflict.
- `plugin-security/src/comment-reaction-own-record-floor.test.ts` runs the shipped `member_default` and a real `SecurityPlugin` over a real engine and driver. It pins that a member creates a reaction on another member's comment and deletes it; that another member cannot delete it, by id (`PERMISSION_DENIED` 403) or by predicate, and the row survives; and that two concurrent reactions each delete only by their reactor.
- `plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.test.ts`: no shipped set carries a row-level policy on `sys_comment_reaction` (a tripwire against a moderation-style alternate).

## Ablations (committed heads `8361ea8d82` and again `32c30d8034`, each through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, disk-verified, restored blob equal to HEAD)

The subjects resolve from source (`plugin-security`'s own `src`, and `plugin-audit`'s own `src` via `./audit-plugin.js`), so no `dist/` sits on the path and no rebuild leg applies.

| leg | mutation | result |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | `owner_only_deletes` object `'*'` changed to an object that does not exist (the own-record floor dropped) | floor test: 2 red (another member's delete answers ok), 1 green |
| A2 | the reaction read middleware's registration deleted | integration test: 9 red (every read pin, including the deleted-comment case), 12 green |
| A3 | the reaction insert hook's registration deleted (run at `8361ea8d82` only) | integration test: setup red (`VALIDATION_FAILED`, `user_id` required, since the stamp is gone), 21 skipped |
| A3b | the comment-readability check short-circuited, stamping kept | integration test: 3 red (both refusal pins, and OTHER's count 4 not 3), 18 green |
| A4 | the app grant's `allowDelete` set to false | floor test: 2 red (the member's own delete refused), 1 green |

On the card's ablation, "drop the own-record row and the first pin goes red": the own-record row is the platform floor, and dropping it (A1) reddens "cannot delete another member's reaction", not the first pin. The first pin rests on the object grant (A4), and the grant's home is the open decision.

## Acceptance notes

- `sys_audit_log` still records every reaction create and delete: the ledger capture is always on, and `activities: false` stops only the `sys_activity` mirror. If the ledger's volume matters, the `SKIP_OBJECTS` set in `audit-writers.ts` is where to change it. That file is not touched here, because PR #22526 holds it.
- A deleted comment's reactions are not removed from storage, and nobody reads them. No cleanup is built, because nothing has named a need for one.
- `comment-access-hooks.ts`'s first header paragraph still says the default member sets "grant wildcard CRUD"; `member_default` has had no wildcard since #5491. This is stale prose, left as it was.
- The `isSystem` census page (`content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`, row 45) describes the comment hooks without naming reactions. Its anchors and counts still hold, and the prose is a docs-only follow-up.
- REST door `PATCH` on the object is NOT MEASURED. The declaration is pinned (`apiMethods` without `update`), and the door's `405` comes from the existing `apiMethods` machinery, not from this diff.
- For objectstack-ai/objectui#12078: create with `comment_id` and `emoji` (`user_id` is stamped and may be omitted). Read with one `find` on `comment_id` `$in` the feed's ids. Remove by deleting the caller's own row by id. A repeated reaction answers 409 `UNIQUE_VIOLATION`.
- The PR owes a contract-review-tier record before the queue (Clause-② yes); the PM arranges it.

## Seat's append: patch round 1 (head `9f26b002a1`)

Appended by `domain:services` seat 1 (`session_013j5gkUCpqQiti4GgPqqmnt`) at 2026-10-10T05:27Z, from the dev's round-1 report (`6094184898` on #22566). Where the sections above describe the object's `apiMethods`, or report results at `32c30d8034`, **this section supersedes them**.

### What this adds: the object (replaces the first bullet)

- **The object** (`plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-comment-reaction.object.ts`, registered beside `sys_comment` in `AuditPlugin.init` and provisioned with it). Fields: `comment_id` (text, at most 255 characters), `emoji` (text, at most 64), `user_id` (lookup to `sys_user`), `created_at`. `apiMethods: ['get', 'list', 'create', 'delete', 'bulk']`; `userActions: { edit: false, import: false }`; `feeds: false`, `activities: false`. No `sharingModel`, and the audit columns are injected, so `created_by` exists and is stamped. `@objectstack/spec`'s platform object registry (`PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['plugin-audit']`) lists it.

### The batch doors (`bulk`)

The object grants `bulk`, as `api-methods-batch-conformance.test.ts` requires of every whitelist that grants single-record writes. It opens no path around the rules above:

- The bulk gate is `bulk ∧ derived(child)`: a batched child is admitted only when it is allowed on its own. `update` is not offered, so `updateMany` and an `upsert` child stay refused.
- `createMany` (`createManyData`) is one `engine.insert` of the rows, and the partial-success batch (`insertManyData`) is `engine.insertMany`. The engine runs `beforeInsert` once per row in both, so every row meets the create gate. Each row is stamped with the session's user, whatever it sent. A row on a comment the caller cannot read refuses the whole batch with `403 RECORD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`, and nothing is written. Pinned in `comment-reaction-access.integration.test.ts` under "bulk create" (3 tests).
- `deleteMany` (`deleteManyData`) deletes one id at a time, by id, so every row meets `owner_only_deletes`. The caller's own reactions are deleted, and another member's fails on its own row (`PERMISSION_DENIED`) and survives. Pinned in `comment-reaction-own-record-floor.test.ts` under "the batch doors keep the own-record floor", driven through the real `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` over the real engine.
- A batched read is an ordinary read, and the read gate narrows it. The reader's `comment_id` `$in` read is the pinned case.
- Ablations at `11e9afaac5`. A1, dropping the floor, reddens the `deleteMany` pin. A3b, short-circuiting the comment-readability check, reddens both bulk-create refusal pins.
